title: After Stop, show figures that are not final as 'at least', up to the root
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: 1. In the stopped tree, every folder the store reports unfinished shows each figure on its row (size, on-disk size, file count) as 'at least': missing
2. Every folder above a 'not read yet' or 'at least' folder, up to and including the root, shows 'at least': missing
3. A folder the store reports final shows its figures with no qualifier: partial
4. The stopped ending's top-level rows carry the same 'at least' marks as the tree: missing
5. In a stopped scan with marks in place, opening a 100k-child folder takes under 0.5 s: partial
6. A scan that runs to the end shows 'at least' nowhere; the existing window cases pass unchanged: partial
Derived (from SC-403, lesson #517): an empty store (Count 0) is guarded before any at-least/unfinished read: partial
Derived (from SC-404): the stopped tree's header says sizes may be off after a Stop in the size checks, worded together with the list header and the rows: missing
Derived (from SC-393 / Q-114): the WindowMutants run covers the App diff, with a mutant that removes the at-least marks: missing
Derived (from 'at least' in the title, and docs/design/SL-112-unfinished-at-stop.md:57-64 and 98-100): the figure marked 'at least' is the store's AtLeast lower bound, not the rolled figure: missing

Cell width: 102 DIP is the measured minimum plus 0.74 DIP. A wider cell (104-106) would buy margin across DPI settings at the Name column's expense. I kept the measured value, with a check that fails on this machine.

T-014 duplicates T-012's protocol with a VOID requirement that marks are realized, instead of extending T-012. Criterion 6 and Q-290 forbid editing T-012, so this is the cost of that rule, not a preference, but a reviewer may prefer one parameterized case.
Four mutants each re-run T-013, about 5-6 min of validate. Two of them, TreeAtLeastRolled and NarrowAtLeastCells, go beyond the derived criterion's single 'remove the marks' mutant.

The marked list row takes its folder and unreadable counts from the tracker row ('at least M folders'), not from a store read. Folder counts only grow, so this is true, but it means the line mixes two sources.
Q-292's follow-up: show each unfinished row's listed figure beside its 'at least' bound after a Stop, labelled as listed and not yet checked, formatted plainly and never through AtLeastSizeText.
A window case for a Stop that lands in the size-check pass (the hook has no trigger inside it): tree and list marks for the few folders whose pending run reaches the watermark.
Check the 102 DIP cells (0.74 DIP margin at 125% DPI) and the tree header's drawn sentence at 100% and 150% DPI and with larger text, which needs a person to change the display scale.
Whole-C: completed scan confirming no NotListed bit survives completion (the blocked spike); criterion 6 on a real drive rests on it, and MarksAtLeast is what stands in front of it meanwhile.
Contain the ending's StoppedTopLevel() call under Q-071's per-pass wrap (review m2, deferred): clear the list and say 'Couldn't show this view', never fall back to the unmarked rows.
Q-276: the stopped list's NotRead row still draws '0 bytes (0 bytes on disk) in 0 files and 0 folders'; its intended wording is undecided.

UnfinishedTests.StopsInTheSizeChecksMarkWhatAPendingCheckCouldChange(workers: 4) failed once in a full-suite run under load ('gb' final with the listing's on-disk figure) and passed every other time; look at whether the 4-worker cutoff has a timing race.
The Q-115 roster guard (WindowMutants' ValidateSet against its -Mutant All list) is still not in the script; the four new names were added to both lists by hand.

deviation: TopLevelSnapshot.WithRows builds the copy through the snapshot's one existing constructor, not through the private copy constructor the design named. tests/bugs/SL-100 finds the snapshot's constructor by reflection as the only non-public one (.Single()), and a second one failed 28 of its 29 facts (lesson #466: the design's consumer check missed tests/bugs). Same behaviour: every field kept, rows cloned.

deviation: Added beyond the design, to discharge O-018 and O-019/O-020: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/AtLeastSeamCorpus.json and AtLeastSeamTests (a reflection and IL census, including a text check of the window's session wiring), docs/design/SL-113-stopped-at-least.md, and plant rows S88-S90/P38-P40 in eng/rules-harness/plants.json (lesson #330).

deviation: The hook's atLeastRealized counts only the opened folder's own realized rows, not every realized row, so the marked root and m-big rows cannot satisfy T-014's void rule by themselves. The cell-fit line is emitted at the end of any Walk (not on WALK=0 runs).

deviation: T-013's NarrowAtLeastCells mutant fails only the cell-fit line, so no MayFail is declared for C1's clipping clause: the stopped fixture's bounds are all 'at least 0 bytes' (79.25 DIP), which fits in 80. The cell-fit line is what catches the widest figure.

deviation: The design's rule list had attempt 1's 'an at least figure is never the rolled or listing figure' removed (it matches AtLeastSize(, which no longer exists); the two settled rules kept and given new 'because' text, and the second states that its two patterns are a tripwire with the IL census as the closure.

deviation: The rule-2 yaml entries sit in .taad/fitness.yaml as the engine appended them in an earlier attempt and as I rewrote them; if the engine appends the declared architecture_rules again at merge the two names may duplicate.

drift: The corpus note in tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/AtLeastSeamCorpus.json says var, target-typed new() and the other spellings 'all compile to the same newobj'. Measured, they compile to call .ctor for struct locals. The design doc repeats that the IL census is the closure (see M1).

drift: Design fact (e) was to run 'on a ragged tree (lesson #511)'. The build runs it on NotListedTests.SweepTree (listing Stops), on the q\a chain tree and on UnfinishedTests.StopTree (size-check Stops), not on NotListedBelowTests.RaggedTree. This was not declared. The q\a tree does give a two-hop NotListedAtOrBelow chain, so propagation is still exercised.

drift: The design named the cell-fit probe 'at least 1,000 bytes'. The hook measures the widest of 'at least ' + FormatSize over every unit, which is 'at least 1,023 bytes'. The width is the same (101.26 DIP). Not declared, and it does no harm.

drift: $T013Needs has extra VOID requirements (b-listed's bound must differ from its rolled figure, and b-listed\b1.bin must be a pending file) beyond the design's two. This strengthens the case and was not declared.

drift: Measured here at 100% DPI with a 1032 DIP work area (the display has changed since the build's 125%/816 DIP runs): the widest figure is still 101.26 DIP in a 102 cell, and the tree header shows 107 characters. This answers part of Q-301's 100% question for this machine. 150% DPI and larger text are still unmeasured.
drift: CheckAtLeastList in WindowCases.ps1 computes $revised and never uses it (dead code, no effect).
not reviewed: .taad/slices/SL-113/*.json (stage records, not code; only index.json read)

not reached: Nonzero 'at least' figures drawn in the window. The hook has no trigger inside the size-check pass, and every Stop during listing gives bound 0. Nonzero bounds were checked in Core on real data (C:\Program Files\dotnet) only, and drawn on screen only through the TreeAtLeastRolled mutant.

not reached: 150% scaling and Windows' larger-text setting. The 102 DIP cells hold 'at least 1,023 bytes' (101.26 DIP) with 0.74 DIP to spare at 100% here and at 125% at build. A person must look, or Q-301's SetRootDpi follow-up must check it.
not reached: At the 560 px minimum width the tree header draws 48 of its characters, so the sentence about the figures is cut. The design claims only the default 880 px.

not reached: A completed scan of the whole C: drive confirming no not-listed mark survives completion (the blocked spike). Criterion 6 on a real drive rests on MarksAtLeast. Completed scans of C:\Program Files\dotnet and the T-013 tree show 0 unfinished.
not reached: Windows 10: no machine here has it.
not reached: StoppedTopLevel's cost inside the App on a 5M-entry stopped store. Spike 126 measured 10.2 ms cold in a Release harness, not in the App's ending.
not reached: The tick-then-ending order (a timer tick showing the final unmarked snapshot before ShowOutcome) was not observed in a window. Only the new-object contract is tested.

critique missed: The design specified TopLevelSnapshot.WithRows through a private copy constructor and listed its consumers as src, tests/window and Core.Tests. tests/bugs/SL-100-ResultsListRefresh finds the snapshot's only non-public constructor by reflection with .Single(), so a second constructor failed 28 of its 29 facts. Neither critique attempt checked tests/bugs consumers. It could have been written as a check: 'grep tests/bugs for GetConstructors/NonPublic on any type whose constructors the design adds or changes' (lesson #466 names this exact gap).

critique missed: Critique attempt 3 accepted M3's 'a type closes the defect class' without asking which spellings of in-place construction inside Core escape fitness rule 2's two patterns. Its own 'because' text already admits a target-typed `return new(...)` escapes. Deferred assignment (`AtLeastFigures forged; forged = new(r.Bytes, r.OnDisk, (int)r.Files);`) in TopLevelTracker.WithAtLeast passed both patterns. The build then added the IL census as 'the closure' and scanned only newobj (0x73). Struct-local construction compiles to call .ctor (0x28). The critique should have asked how a non-store Core method can construct the bound and what proves it fails.

critique missed: The kept rule 'the at-least word is composed only in TopLevelRowText' and its 'because' text ('the only way to put the word on a number') were never tested against split-line, local-variable or pre-formatted-string spellings, or against XAML StringFormat. The rule reads only App *.cs, one line at a time. The design's rule 2 was worded as a tripwire, but rule 1 was not. Critique 3 re-checked the M3 type closure and did not re-attack the surviving text rule.

still unknown: Whether the engine re-appends the declared architecture_rules at merge on top of the rule-2 entries already hand-placed in .taad/fitness.yaml. The build flagged possible duplicate names, and nothing before the commit stage has checked it.
still unknown: Whether a real completed whole-C: scan leaves any NotListed bit set. Criterion 6 on a real drive rests only on ScanResult.MarksAtLeast; the spike is still blocked on a person's OK.

still unknown: StoppedTopLevel's cost inside the running App on a 5M-entry stopped store. Spike 126 measured 10.2 ms cold in a Release harness, not in the App's ending, which already spends 196-293 ms on LargestFiles.Top(100).

still unknown: Whether a timer tick can draw the final unmarked snapshot before ShowOutcome and then be replaced by the marked copy without a visible flicker or lost selection. Only the new-object contract is tested; the tick-then-ending order was never observed in a window.
still unknown: Whether the 4-worker size-check cutoff has a real timing race (the single UnfinishedTests failure). The candidate asks for a looped reproduction.

Attempt 3 chose a UI-thread read nobody had measured cold, which forced a re-synthesis and a third spike before attempt 4. Two of those laps were avoidable with earlier questions and an earlier timing ask.
went wrong: Code review ran five times, and attempts 1-3 refused (provider errors). The 32-file diff was first read at attempt 4, so three laps passed with no review.

went wrong: The IL census added beyond the design to discharge O-018 shipped with a false measured-sounding claim ('var, target-typed new() ... all compile to the same newobj') and scanned only 0x73. The design doc repeated 'the IL census is the closure'. This is the spelling-class overclaim lesson #486 warned about. Two of the code review's findings (O-037 census, O-038 rule 1) were again spelling-class in a rule or census written in this slice, and both were waived to the backlog (SC-423, SC-424).

went wrong: The design named a private copy constructor for TopLevelSnapshot.WithRows. It broke 28 of 29 facts in tests/bugs/SL-100 and was reworked in build. Lesson #466 had already named the tests/bugs consumer-grep gap and the design's consumer check missed it again.

went wrong: A full-suite failure of an SL-112 test under load (UnfinishedTests ... workers: 4, 'gb' final with listing figures) was recorded as 'a timing flake ... not investigated further' with no evidence it was one. That same symptom is the one the new 'unmarked is final' header promises cannot happen.

went wrong: Validate wrote the ragged-tree propagation sweep and a real-data size-check Stop test as temporary files and deleted them. The strongest evidence for the imported precondition (2,447 ancestor checks) is not in the repo, while the design's named RaggedTree run was silently swapped for other trees during the build.

went wrong: Nonzero 'at least' figures were never drawn on screen except through a mutant, because the hook has no Stop trigger inside the size-check pass. The slice shipped with the nonzero draw path covered only by Core tests.

went wrong: The stopped list's NotRead rows still draw '0 bytes (0 bytes on disk) in 0 files and 0 folders' unmarked beside a header that now says 'a row with no mark is final'. This was left deliberately under open Q-276, but it is the one place the slice goal ('any figure without a mark is final') is read loosely, and T-013 pins it as 'unworded'.

caused_by.reason: Trip 1 of 2 back to the risk spike: the design left 1 fork that only a measurement can settle. O-002: unsettled design fork: Does the ending's StoppedTopLevel read (Unfinished + AtLeast for every root child, about one pass over the pending range) stay well within one UI frame budget on a 5M-entry store stopped in the listing? Its context: This design puts it on the UI thread at the ending. U-205 measured the read of every folder at 5M at 54.7-71.3 ms, and SL-112 measured the read form at <= 12 ms for one folder at 5M, so the root's children should cost well under 100 ms. Nothing has measured it inside the App. If it takes hundreds of ms, the read moves into Scanner.Finish on the writing thread after the watermark is written: a component boundary and risk-tier change. The synthesis marked this as forcing a re-synthesis: the losing answer moves a component boundary, a contract or the data model. How the fork decider would measure it: MEASURE on the risk spike before the design is rewritten. No code needs building first: time the exact store work that ScanResult.StoppedTopLevel() will do. SETUP: use the 5M-entry generated store that UnfinishedBudgetTests / NotListedBudgetTests already build. That is 4,880,000 entries in scanner (depth-first, one SetChildren per block) order, with the 100,000-child folder. Set the size-check watermark the way Scanner.Finish sets it after a Stop in the listing, which is 0. Then repeat at 50% and 97% of Count. THE TIMED WORK: in a FRESH process, with no warm-up call (the App's ending makes the first call cold, at tier-0 JIT), time this loop: if Count > 0, for i = FirstChild(0) .. FirstChild(0)+ChildCount(0)-1: NotListed(i) Unfinished(i) AtLeast(i) when Unfinished && !NotListed RUNS: - Release build: this is the shipped App's config and the number that decides. - Debug build: record it alongside. - 3 cold processes per cutoff, run one after another (about 650 MiB each). - If the generator's root children are roughly even in size, add one run where a single root child holds at least 70% of the entries (real C:'s Users shape). RECORD per run: - ms for the loop - number of root children and number marked - bytes allocated - as calibration, in the same process, LargestFiles.Top(100) over the same store. That is the whole-store pass the ending already runs on the UI thread. HOW THE RESULT DECIDES THE FORK. The deciding number is the Release cold max at every cutoff. (a) At or under 250 ms (the bar UnfinishedBudgetTests.cs:185 already sets for App-facing reads): keep the design as written. StoppedTopLevel() runs on the UI thread at the ending (MainWindow.xaml.cs:301, `result?.StoppedTopLevel()`). Scanner.cs is not touched and the slice's risk tier does not change. (b) Over 250 ms at any cutoff: move the read into Scanner.Finish, after the size-check watermark is written. Finish calls TopLevelTracker.WithAtLeast, and ScanResult carries the marked snapshot. StoppedTopLevel() returns that snapshot without reading the store, so the public contract is unchanged. The slice is re-tiered as scanner-touching, and Stop-to-return latency is measured again. The 16 ms frame in the question's title is NOT the bar. The ending is a one-time transition that already runs whole-store passes on the UI thread (LargestFiles.Top took 37-53 ms at 4.9M in U-137). The design's own switch point is 'hundreds of ms'. Nobody has measured this read, and both sides of the fork are outcomes of that missing measurement. What exists are proxies: - Build-check: Unfinished+AtLeast for every row of one 100k-child folder took 29.5 ms (Debug), and the same reads for every entry of the 5M store took 651 ms (Debug). - U-205: a boolean pending read over every folder took 54.7-71.3 ms (Release). - SL-112: R took ≤12 ms for one folder whose identity is not recorded here. Under depth-first registration the root children's pending runs are disjoint, so the read should cost about one pass over the store: tens of ms. But the only figure that strictly contains this read (651 ms, Debug) sits across the 'hundreds of ms' line, and none of the proxies was a cold first call, which is what the ending makes. The measurement is cheap and can be done on this machine without a person: minutes of time and about 650 MiB per process, using a generator that is already in the suite. The losing answer moves a component into the scanner tier, which is the case a lap exists for. Guessing 'UI thread' and being wrong would ship a stall that no planned case catches, because T-014's fixture is about 100k entries, not 5M. Either outcome keeps ScanResult.StoppedTopLevel() as the public seam, so the redesign after the measurement stays contained. The risk spike measures these first. Write the design again with what it measured: its experiments are under what reality already said about this slice.
